## Question

Can a small relational graph neural network (R-GCN), trained on a laptop CPU
in a few minutes, rank known drug–disease treatment links in Hetionet
[@himmelstein2017] better than a simple common-neighbour baseline? This report
describes the data. The model and the baseline will be added in later lessons.

## Data

```{python}
#| label: setup
import sys

import matplotlib
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import pandas as pd

from scripts.hetionet import edge_types, load_edges, load_nodes

nodes = load_nodes()
edges = load_edges()
types = edge_types(edges)
```

Hetionet v1.0 [@hetionet_data] has `{python} f"{len(nodes):,}"` nodes of
`{python} f"{nodes['kind'].nunique()}"` types (@tbl-nodes) and
`{python} f"{len(edges):,}"` edges of `{python} f"{len(types)}"` types
(@tbl-edges).

```{python}
#| label: tbl-nodes
#| tbl-cap: "Nodes of each type."
nodes["kind"].value_counts().rename_axis("node type").reset_index(name="nodes")
```

```{python}
#| label: tbl-edges
#| tbl-cap: "Edges of each type: the metaedge abbreviation, the node types it connects and the number of edges."
types
```

## Known treatments

```{python}
#| label: ctd
ctd = edges[edges["metaedge"] == "CtD"]
per_compound = ctd["source"].value_counts()
per_disease = ctd["target"].value_counts()
n_compounds = (nodes["kind"] == "Compound").sum()
n_diseases = (nodes["kind"] == "Disease").sum()
```

The model will predict the Compound–treats–Disease (CtD) edges. There are
`{python} f"{len(ctd)}"` of them, linking `{python} f"{per_compound.size}"` of
the `{python} f"{n_compounds:,}"` compounds and `{python} f"{per_disease.size}"`
of the `{python} f"{n_diseases}"` diseases. Most of these compounds
(`{python} f"{(per_compound == 1).sum()}"`) treat a single disease, while the
number of known treatments per disease ranges from 1 to
`{python} f"{per_disease.max()}"` (@fig-ctd). A model can therefore score well
by ranking the diseases that already have many treatments, which the
evaluation will have to take into account.

```{python}
#| label: fig-ctd
#| fig-cap: "Known treatments (CtD edges) per compound (left) and per disease (right), for the compounds and diseases that have at least one."
#| fig-alt: "Two histograms. Left: diseases treated per compound, from 1 to 19; about two thirds of the compounds treat one disease and the bars fall quickly after that. Right: known treatments per disease, from 1 to 68; the bars are spread over 1 to 16 treatments, with a tall bar at 1, and a sparse tail of about ten diseases between 21 and 68."
fig, (left, right) = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(8, 3.2))
left.hist(per_compound, bins=range(1, per_compound.max() + 2), color="#2a78d6")
left.set_xlabel("Diseases treated per compound")
left.set_ylabel("Compounds")
right.hist(per_disease, bins=range(1, per_disease.max() + 2), color="#eb6834")
right.set_xlabel("Known treatments per disease")
right.set_ylabel("Diseases")
fig.tight_layout()
plt.show()
```
